title: TE Robert G. Rayburn et al. v. Missouri Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint not sustained 7-4; motion to sustain specifications of error failed 4-7-0; lower court decision confirmed 7-4-0; statement of facts and issue adopted 10-0-0; explanatory statement adopted 6-0-4; commendation adopted 10-0-0; report adopted by 16th General Assembly 238-191. A dissent was filed and printed.
first_summary: The Judicial Commission denied a complaint against Missouri Presbytery's April 16, 1988 instructions for examining candidates. It confirmed the lower court's action. The majority relied on the absence of a specific candidate, the safeguards in the motion, ongoing theological debate, and the value of grass-roots resolution. The dissent argued that the qualified minority view on prophecy and tongues was fundamentally out of accord with PCA doctrine, citing earlier Bogue and Gentry decisions.
summary: Missouri Presbytery instructed its Candidates and Credentials Committee to examine candidates without treating a qualified minority view on prophecy and tongues as disqualifying. Complainants argued this conflicted with the 1986 Gentry decision. The Judicial Commission, adopted by the 16th General Assembly, did not sustain the complaint and confirmed the lower court 7-4. Although earlier similar cases had annulled lower-court actions, it cited the absence of a specific candidate, safeguards, inconclusive debate, and a preference for grass-roots resolution, encouraging Overture 25. The dissent called the view fundamentally out of accord.

evidence_notes.qualifications: Lines 83-106 state the majority's reluctance because prior similar decisions annulled lower-court actions, no specific individual was involved, the action had safeguards, debate was inconclusive, and grass-roots resolution was preferred; the Assembly was encouraged to act on Overture 25.
